title: Naturality of localized beta on integral pure tensors
statement: Fix the finite-field, prime, scheme, coefficient extensions, dualizing data, rational Verdier data, family c and component equations of [lem-coef-rational-verdier-comparison-naturality]. For integral constructible objects K and M, an integral coefficient a and an integral arrow f, the localized beta naturality equation holds for the pure tensor a tensor f. This is the integral pure-tensor subcase used to prove the rational statement.

source.place: paragraph 3, integral-arrow transpose and pure tensor calculation

proof.text: For arbitrary tensor-Hom adjunctions, uncurry composition with internal-Hom precomposition. The first-variable evaluation naturality equation and tensor functoriality identify this with tensoring the source arrow before uncurrying. Apply this to the evaluation transpose defining homMap. Naturality of the inverse scalar tensorator in each argument, followed by the source evaluation naturality equation, proves first-variable naturality of homMap.

source.place: paragraph 3, integral-arrow transpose and pure tensor calculation

proof.text: Use naturality of completedScalarComparison and cancellation of its invertible components to move source arrows across the inverse completion maps. Functoriality of the target internal Hom moves the same square through its contravariant completion inverse and covariant completion map. Conjugating homMap naturality gives v naturality. Postcomposition with internal Hom into the fixed dualizing arrow u commutes with precomposition, so beta is natural on integral arrows.

source.place: paragraph 3, integral-arrow transpose and pure tensor calculation

proof.text: Use the object and pure-tensor equations of A.dual, B.dual and rational scalar extension. They identify the two mapped arrows with the image of the coefficient tensored with the corresponding integral dual and scalar arrows. The supplied equations hc identify the comparison components with one tensored with beta. The raw-localization composition formula reduces the desired equation to the image coefficient tensored with integral beta naturality. No faithfulness of localization or finite reduction is used.
